2. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that earlier application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. by the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 11810/2024 with liberty to revive his prayer at appropriate stage in future.

Thereafter, an application bearing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55324 2 CRA-10605-2024 I.A.No.28629/2024 for amendment has been filed which was allowed on 04.11.2024 and this M.Cr.C. has been converted into Criminal Appeal.
It is contended by the counsel that at the time of consideration of the present applicant's previous application which was withdrawn with liberty, the statement of the prosecutrix could not be read.

sentences.text: applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail as he is suffering incarceration since 15.02.2024.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-State contends that the present appeal for bail deserves to be dismissed.
It is contended by the counsel that the prosecutrix has supported the allegation which is evident from paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of her testimony.

It is further contended by the counsel that the prosecutrix was stranger to the present applicant, therefore, there was no question of any kind of consent and the offence of rape was committed by the present applicant.
Thus, taking into consideration the nature of offence, the appeal for grant of bail is not made out.

4. Heard rival submissions of both the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

On perusal of the case diary prima facie reflects that the prosecutrix had boarded a train and in which, the prosecutrix met with the present applicant who committed rape upon her on the toilet of M.T. Rack train.
The prosecutrix has supported the allegation of commission of offence in paragraph 3 and 4 of her testimony.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55324 3 CRA-10605-2024 6.
Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and also looking to the statement of the prosecutrix, it would not be appropriate to release the appellant on bail.
7. Accordingly, the present appeal stands dismissed.
